clue.text: Tailless tree bird seen around lake

parts.note: the tit is a small garden bird

indicators.note: seen around says the shortened tree is turned to face the other way
tailless says the word for the tree loses its final letter

parts.note: the acacia is a tree, often called wattle

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted circling a lake beside a tree that has lost its top or end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' and 'seen around' both work on the tree; the bird stands in front of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Titicaca is the large high-altitude lake on the border of Peru and Bolivia.

clue.text: One examines a canopy

definitions.meaning: someone who checks or tries things out
a canopy over a four-poster bed

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a canopy.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner of things, and also the old word for the canopy over a bed or pulpit.

clue.text: Thanks to strike is stuck on island — this one?

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
to strike is to hit

explanation.surface: A grateful visitor hits upon an island and asks if this is the one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this one?' points back to the island in the wordplay: the answer is itself an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is the largest island of French Polynesia in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Happen to be a locum working without licence initially

indicators.note: working says these letters are set going in a fresh order
without says a letter is taken away from the phrase
initially picks the first letter of the word licence

explanation.surface: A stand-in doctor ends up practising without a licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops L from TO BE A LOCUM, and 'working' rearranges TOBEAOCUM.
explanation.definitionFit: To occur or take place, as an idiom for an event arising.

clue.text: Usual residence for sisters overlooks island on lake

indicators.note: overlooks says the first piece sits above the rest in this down entry

parts.note: nuns, religious sisters, live in a convent
Iona is a small island of the Inner Hebrides, off western Scotland

explanation.surface: A nunnery's usual home looks out over an island on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Following normal custom or accepted practice, so ordinary or standard.

clue.text: A day to get round Scottish town

parts.note: Thurs is the usual short form of Thursday, one day of the week
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone needs a whole day to travel round a Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Thurso is a town on the far north coast of Scotland, in Caithness.

clue.text: Cheer up, Mum! That's unkind

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rah is a cheer, as in hurrah
mum as in keep quiet, so the call for silence sh

explanation.surface: Telling Mum to cheer up seems a bit unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother; it is 'mum's the word', silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe, cruel or rough in manner is the opposite of gentle or kind.

clue.text: Virginia's brought in to soften material

indicators.note: brought in says the state's letters are placed inside the other word

parts.note: to relent is to soften one's stance
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Virginia is called in to make some fabric softer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like fabric; it is the adjective, pertinent.
explanation.definitionFit: Material evidence is pertinent evidence, bearing on the matter in hand.

clue.text: Ground elder on a shrub

indicators.note: ground as in crushed in a mill, so the letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: Crushed elderflowers are laid on a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground elder' is a garden weed, a false trail; 'Ground' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is a poisonous evergreen flowering bush of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Composer's friend breaking largely sad news

indicators.note: breaking says the friend splits the other letters apart
largely means most of the word sad, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a chum is a friend
news read as new things, two Ns each standing for new

explanation.surface: A composer's companion interrupts with mostly gloomy tidings.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay; news is read as two Ns for 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Schumann was a German Romantic composer of songs, piano works and symphonies.

clue.text: Cook needs last of cheese for grating

parts.note: to cook under direct heat is to grill

indicators.note: last of picks out the final letter of the word cheese

explanation.surface: A recipe step: to cook this, you need the end of the cheese for grating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grating' looks like what you do to cheese; it is the noun, a metal grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A grille is a grating or lattice of bars, as over a window or in a car's front.

clue.text: Not answering mobile so unnerves one holding power

indicators.note: mobile means moving freely, so these letters are shifted about
holding says the stirred letters take in the power symbol as well, so it lands among them

parts.note: one as the Roman numeral I
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A mobile phone rings without reply, which rattles someone with authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' looks like a phone; it is the anagram signal for SO UNNERVES with I, and 'holding' puts P among those letters, as the blog reads it.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving no reply or reaction, as a person who does not respond.

clue.text: Stretch of Spandex tracksuit is wide?

indicators.note: Stretch of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asks whether a stretchy Spandex tracksuit is roomy.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'is wide' does not swap for a noun; 'wide' alone is the cricket term, with 'is' a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a wide, a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, adds a run as a bonus to the score.

clue.text: I need empty house, just outside Dutch city

indicators.note: outside says the word for just goes around the other pieces

parts.note: just as in fair or level means even

indicators.note: empty says the word need loses its inside, keeping only its ends

explanation.surface: Someone needs a vacant house just outside a Dutch city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps only the outer letters of 'need'; HO is the usual abbreviation for house.
explanation.definitionFit: Eindhoven is a city in the southern Netherlands, home of Philips and PSV.

clue.text: Naturally she's not fair to belle, mostly — don't be upset

indicators.note: upset says the letters gathered here are knocked into a new order
mostly means the word belle without its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone pleads with a beauty not to be upset that she is not truly fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts BELLE to BELL; 'upset' rearranges TO + BELL + DONTBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose fair hair comes from peroxide rather than nature is said to have dyed it out of a bottle.

clue.text: Northbound rail out of one poor city district is rather slow

indicators.note: northbound in a down entry means the letters run upwards, reversed
out of says a letter is removed from the word rail

parts.note: one as the Roman numeral I
a ghetto is a poor, deprived part of a city

explanation.surface: A northbound train service runs slowly through a deprived neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' drops I from RAIL to give RAL, which 'Northbound' turns into LAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Larghetto is a musical tempo marking, a little faster than largo but still slowish.

clue.text: Prone to lose rights, supporting a renegade

indicators.note: supporting says the trimmed word sits under the a in this down entry
to lose says those letters drop out of the word

parts.note: prone means lying flat, prostrate
R stands for right, so rights are two Rs

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to give up their rights backs a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' removes both Rs from PROSTRATE, leaving POSTATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abandons a religious faith or cause is a renegade or defector.

clue.text: Time to chuck it in, having good education

parts.note: to chuck it down is to rain heavily

explanation.surface: Someone decides to quit after a good education.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chuck it in' looks like giving up; 'chuck it' alone means pour with rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Instruction that teaches a skill or prepares someone is schooling or education.

clue.text: Soldiers desert with Joey, wearing rags

indicators.note: wearing says the inner pieces are clothed by the outer word

parts.note: rags is slang for newspapers, papers
to desert is to rat, abandon one's side
a joey is a baby kangaroo, a roo

explanation.surface: Troops abandon their posts with a youngster dressed in tatters.
explanation.walkthrough: A joey is a young kangaroo, and 'rags' is a disparaging word for newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Paratroopers are soldiers trained to drop into action by parachute.

clue.text: Place fit for dog

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
an ague is a fit of fever and shivering

explanation.surface: A spot that is suitable for a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' looks like the animal; it is the verb, to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to pester or trouble them persistently.

clue.text: Uniform feeds public image

indicators.note: feeds says the letter is put into the other word

parts.note: public as in of the state, state-run
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A uniform shapes the public face of an organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'public image' looks like reputation; 'image' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved or cast figure of a person is an image or effigy.

clue.text: How to make Aryan tell story?

definitions.meaning: spinning, or rearranging, the word Aryan gives the two words a yarn, so the instruction describes this
to relate a long, perhaps embroidered tale

explanation.surface: Asks how to turn someone into an Aryan, a sinister-sounding question.
explanation.walkthrough: SPIN reads as an anagram instruction, and spinning the letters of ARYAN gives A YARN.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating a long, often embroidered tale is a common idiom for storytelling.

clue.text: Speak ill of topless dress

indicators.note: topless says the word loses its top letter, its first in this down entry

parts.note: to malign someone is to speak ill of them

explanation.surface: Criticism of a topless outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' looks like clothing; it is the military verb for lining up troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress ranks is to put soldiers in a straight line, arranging them evenly.

clue.text: One enthralled the man a great deal

parts.note: a man is referred to as he
a lot means a great deal

explanation.surface: A captivated person greatly admired the man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enthralled' suggests charmed; here it means held in thrall, enslaved.
explanation.definitionFit: A helot was a serf of ancient Sparta, so a person in bondage.

clue.text: Detectives tucked into excellent cold tart

indicators.note: tucked into says the detectives go inside the word for excellent

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as A and I
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's police detectives
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Police officers tuck into a fine chilled pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like a pastry; it is the adjective, sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sharp and sour to taste, like lemon juice, is tart.

clue.text: Impenetrable island shelters right criminal

indicators.note: shelters says the island goes around the other letters

parts.note: an ait is a small river island

indicators.note: criminal means the word right is bent out of shape

explanation.surface: An island fortress hides a dangerous criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges RIGHT to RTIGH, which 'shelters' puts in AIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealed so nothing can get in, as a well-argued case with no loophole is.

clue.text: Machine gun originally seen in middle of Red Square

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letter of the word Red
seen in says that letter sits within the other pieces

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of the word gun

explanation.surface: A machine gun is spotted in the middle of Red Square in Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Machine gun' looks like one phrase; only 'Machine' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor or mechanical device that converts energy into motion is a machine.

clue.text: In Kentucky, got higher energy fuel

indicators.note: In says the word for got higher goes inside the state's short form

parts.note: Ken is an old abbreviation for the US state of Kentucky
rose means went up, got higher
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone in Kentucky moved on to a higher-energy fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin oil, burned in lamps, heaters and jet engines, is a fuel.
